statusDefinitions.SUPPORTED: The listed evidence supports the claim within its stated scope.
statusDefinitions.PARTIAL: The listed evidence supports only part of the claim; limitations identify the unsupported portion.
statusDefinitions.UNMEASURED: No benchmark or representative measured dataset supports the claim.
statusDefinitions.NOT_CLAIMED: The capability is explicitly outside the current submission claim set.

evidenceClassDefinitions.mainnet_observation: A time-bound read from a mainnet network.
evidenceClassDefinitions.testnet_observation: A time-bound read or interaction on a test network.
evidenceClassDefinitions.historical_replay: A result produced by replaying a fixed historical dataset.
evidenceClassDefinitions.synthetic_fixture: A deterministic result produced from controlled fixture data.
evidenceClassDefinitions.publisher_claim: A statement or status returned by the operator's own service.

claims.claim: The repository-tested no-resubmission recovery kernel was deployed behind an explicitly enabled read-only gate in release 35def38e730e. The API and worker were healthy, five public checks returned HTTP 200, and two worker samples saw an empty chain-action queue with zero claimed, examined, changed, or failed actions. A separate in-memory invocation inside the deployed worker image observed existing BSC testnet transaction 0xee8c816faceaea83f0eb9745e72230bde2190f439a4cac9ef8181162d54582bf as SUCCESS at block 130060913 with 11022 confirmations through the known-hash observer; it did not use the database, wallet, queue, broadcaster, or any chain-write path.

scope.recoveryClaimStrategy: parent job lease with fencing token and FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
scope.transactionLocator: journaled transaction hash with exact nonce binding
scope.workerWiring: opt-in and explicitly enabled in the captured deployment
scope.shutdownBehavior: abort active observation without outcome rewrite and release the exact fenced job lease

limitations: The deployed queue was empty, so no queued receipt observation, lease, reconciliation transition, recovery retry, or recovery effectiveness was exercised.
One isolated in-memory known-hash probe observed an existing BSC testnet transaction through the deployed observer and safe read transport; it did not use the database, wallet, or queue.
The receipt probe is one point-in-time testnet observation and does not establish repeatability, provider redundancy, reorg-after-terminal handling, or lost-hash recovery.
The public checks and two worker samples do not establish uptime, an SLA, load capacity, regional availability, or host recovery.
No transaction broadcaster or automatic resubmission path exists, and no chain write or fund transfer was performed.
Relay and account-abstraction recovery remain outside scope.

claims.claim: One BSC testnet session was granted only U.balanceOf(address) call authority plus a 0.005 tBNB hourly native spend cap, successfully exercised that read, rejected totalSupply(), was revoked, and then rejected the formerly allowed read without changing the U balance or commerce allowance.
limitations: This claim covers one bounded BSC testnet session and no mainnet transaction or real funds.
The session could read one test-token function but could not transfer or approve tokens.
The native spend cap covered testnet relay fees and did not authorize ERC-20 spending.
Rejected calls failed during simulation and therefore have no transaction hashes.
One completed grant-and-revoke cycle is not a production-security or reliability guarantee.

claims.claim: Pinned Slither 0.11.3 output plus team manual validation on Shield's hash-frozen six-fixture corpus produced 2 true positives, 0 false positives, and 7 false negatives across 9 adjudicated findings; the ERC-1967 holdout produced 0 true positives, 0 false positives, and 3 false negatives.
limitations: All fixtures and adjudicated labels are team-owned, so this is not an independent external benchmark.
Manual validation is part of the measured pipeline and rejected two mapped analyzer signals before scoring, so the reported false-positive count is post-validation.
Ground-truth labels were not supplied to Slither; the evaluator consumed separately produced and hash-preserved artifacts.
The corpus contains only six synthetic fixtures, and its 2/9 recall and 0/3 holdout result do not establish comprehensive audit quality.
No production-security, deployment, or on-chain execution result is claimed.

claims.claim: The repository-tested public seller verifier resolves every outbound HTTPS hostname, rejects a resolution set containing any non-public address, pins an accepted address for the TLS connection, refuses redirects at this call site, enforces request and response size limits, and applies one total wall-clock deadline across resolution, redirects, and response transfer.
limitations: Only call sites that use this boundary receive these protections; unrelated network clients require separate migration and review.
The frozen cases are deterministic synthetic controls and do not represent every DNS or network topology.
Destination controls and byte limits do not establish upstream correctness, availability, or application authorization.

claims.claim: One paid paired experiment is published for each of KNOT's four finance categories. The agent and non-agent reference paths used the same frozen input within each pair, and independent evaluators reproduced four quality ties: HealthGuard across 4 dimensions, RangePilot across 6, GridQuant across 5, and YieldScout across 5.
limitations: Each quality tie covers one input and does not establish superiority or repeatability.

RangePilot, GridQuant, and YieldScout use later historical-replay baselines; HealthGuard uses calculation-only timing. None of the baseline measurements is timing-comparable to the full agent lifecycle.

HealthGuard's two paths share the same separately SHA-256-bound committed input, but its TaskSpec input hash does not match those raw bytes; no authentic signed-task preimage binding is claimed for that pair.
All four sellers and reference implementations are operated by KNOT; evaluator independence means scores are recomputed from raw evidence, not independent business ownership.
No speed, human-time, cost, profit, APY, return, savings, PnL, win-rate, execution, or live-trading advantage is claimed.

claims.claim: Release bf2738478888 deployed a private byte-exact service-request intake boundary. The API and worker were healthy on the same immutable image, migration 0008 was present in an eight-migration database, the new table was empty at observation time, five public health or agent-card checks returned HTTP 200, and an unauthenticated service-request attempt returned HTTP 401.
limitations: No authenticated service request was created in the deployed environment, so the live observation does not prove the authenticated write path end to end.
No seller negotiation, payment, wallet operation, chain RPC call, transaction, mainnet write, or frontend change was performed.
The seller-schema compatibility gate covers a declared adversarial matrix and exact retained fixtures; the marketplace and seller schemas are not yet one canonical package.
Raw request bytes are append-only without retention or crypto-erasure, so the deployed intake is limited to bounded testnet and demo inputs rather than production private portfolio data.
Five point-in-time HTTP responses and service health states do not establish uptime, load capacity, an SLA, regional behavior, or disaster recovery.

claims.claim: Release 80e3b45 completed one authenticated KNOT-operated RangePilot quote-only flow with dual-RPC confirmed ERC-8004 identity, a verified EIP-191 quote, atomic append-only persistence, and an immutable retry while keeping jobs, wallets, funding, and chain writes disabled.
limitations: This is one KNOT-operated RangePilot quote-only observation, not a paid hire, independently operated seller, delivery, settlement, uptime, load, failover, or SLA result.
The quote route has no wallet action, job creation, funding, notification, settlement, or chain-write connection and explicitly returns fundingPermitted false.
The repository persists EIP-191 EOA quotes; ERC-1271 remains unresolved until a pinned-block network verifier is implemented.
The identity observation was obtained from two pinned BSC testnet RPC providers at one confirmed block; it does not establish future owner, endpoint, or provider availability.
Two pre-fix attempts retained their task and service-request inputs but correctly created no quote, observation, job, outbox item, or chain action when exact endpoint binding failed.
GridQuant job 1187, YieldScout job 1188, and RangePilot job 1189 predate mandatory request-ID replay binding and are intentionally rejected by the new verifier.
Append-only service-request and quote data have no retention or crypto-erasure mechanism.

claims.claim: One unaided operator with no prior familiarity solved the frozen yield-comparison task in 1110431 ms of recorder-measured wall clock and reached the same recommendation, decision and net-benefit value as the paid YieldScout job, whose recorded lifecycle was 148373 ms.
limitations: One operator on one task. A single observation supports no population claim and no average.

The time boundaries are not identical. The agent window runs from recorded marketplace start through confirmed on-chain submission and includes block inclusion; the operator window covers task work only.
Costs are testnet U and tBNB. Testnet units are not dollars and no monetary break-even or hourly rate is claimed.
The operator answered from the identical frozen snapshot, so this measures effort on a fixed historical input and not live market work.

A separate AI-assisted run of the same task is retained but excluded from every human-effort claim, and two earlier attempts whose timing could not be verified are quarantined and published as evidence of nothing.
